decision: Pilot stopped at step 1,950 (~$0.52). Do not scale the run. Determine whether the validation pool is structurally unlike the training pool for the atom families, or whether those families genuinely do not transfer across source molecules.
finding: Bimodal and clean: four families at +2.86 to +4.55 nats, four at -0.34 to +0.33. The four with large gaps are 72.8% of the training draw. They FIT training well (atom_delete 2.42 against a 4.79 uniform baseline) and are WORSE than uniform held out (6.64). So the failure is transfer, not budget: more epochs widen this rather than closing it.
note_on_the_curve: Trend claims on the eval series were made twice and refuted twice. The law-weighted mean oscillates 5.7-6.2 with no direction, and it is structurally the noisiest metric available because it reweights small per-family panel means by large law shares. This finding rests on the train-vs-held-out LEVEL comparison, which does not depend on the trajectory.
why_it_was_invisible: The aggregate held-out NLL (4.42) looks reasonable because the panel is 62.6% cycle_insert and cycle_attach, which generalize almost perfectly, while the law-heavy families that fail are the panel's thinnest strata. Reporting only the panel-native mean would have hidden this entirely.
